analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 10.2.26
key_insights: Futures are bid ahead of September payrolls (Nasdaq +75bps, S&P +50bps). WTI is down 4% and the 10-year yield is 5.23%, slightly off its highs. GS estimates nonfarm payrolls rose 80k in September vs consensus +88k.

STX fell 11% and WDC fell 7% premarket on a Nikkei report that Toshiba will invest about ¥60bn ($380M) to double hard disk drive production capacity within fiscal 2027. Toshiba holds just over 10% of HDD capacity share and targets 30% in the medium term.
Toshiba's Philippines expansion is its first major HDD investment in around five years. New products would raise per-unit capacity by as much as 40%.
ON rose 8% premarket after amending its Synaptics acquisition to about $5.7bn in cash ($123 per share) from about $7bn in stock. ON says the deal is immediately accretive to EPS.
ON revised the Synaptics terms after an unsolicited competing proposal from an unnamed third party.
APP fell 5% premarket on another negative sell-side note. The stock is lower in 13 of its last 14 sessions.
TWLO rose 1.5% on news it will join the S&P 500 on October 6, replacing Warner Bros. Discovery.

FT reports Amazon is seeking to offload about $8bn of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors' debt, and would lease the chips back. This would make its balance sheet more asset-light.
AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon named Paul Roth interim CEO of their satellite coverage joint venture. Some analysts see the venture as defensive against SpaceX's Starlink mobile ambitions.
SpaceX acquired 65 MHz of wireless spectrum from EchoStar for $19.6bn through two deals announced last year.
Crude is falling on reports that European countries are discussing releasing diesel stockpiles, with France suggesting 100mb of diesel plus crude (FT/BBG).
Eurozone headline CPI was slightly hotter and core was in line. Tokyo CPI printed very hot across the board.

GS maintains a Sell on Adobe. Anil Chakravarthy becomes CEO on 12/1, Wadhwani is stepping down and a permanent CFO is being appointed. GS sees new leadership as a catalyst but wants visibility into strategic decisions and execution first.
GS read-across from Micron's 4QFY26 print: MU expects CY27 and CY28 memory supply/demand to be much tighter than CY26. GS reiterates Buy on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
South Korea September DRAM exports hit an all-time high of US$33bn (+552% yoy). Memory exports rose +359% yoy, the 8th straight month above +200%.

market_movers.rationale: New CEO is a possible catalyst, but competition is intensifying and TAM growth is accruing to new entrants. GS wants visibility into strategic decisions and execution.
Samsung Electronics: Micron's print points to tighter CY27-CY28 memory supply/demand, higher HBM pricing in 2027 and longer, larger supply commitments.
SK Hynix: same Micron read-across, including significantly higher HBM pricing in 2027, in line with GS expectations.
Shares fell 11% premarket on Toshiba's plan to double HDD capacity.
Shares fell 7% premarket on the same Toshiba capacity news.
Shares rose 8% premarket after the Synaptics deal was changed to all cash and is immediately accretive to EPS.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees alpha over the next 12 months in software companies that move from 'AI loser' to 'AI winner'. Consensus expects AI headwinds for Adobe.
Micron expects CY27 and CY28 supply/demand to be much tighter than 2026, with HBM pricing rising significantly in 2027.

earnings_insights: Micron reported 4QFY26 (June-August) results on September 30. DRAM ASP growth was in line with GS estimates for SEC/Hynix and NAND ASP growth was higher than GS's 3Q26 estimates.
Micron signed 10 additional supply commitment agreements (SCAs), with customers asking for longer duration and larger supply. It plans additional capex to prepare for beyond 2028.
ON says the revised Synaptics deal is immediately accretive to its EPS (no figure given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly below consensus of +88k in the text, while the events line lists consensus at +100k. The report gives two different consensus figures.
Consensus figure cited in the opening paragraph.

macro_indicators.indicator: US September nonfarm payrolls (consensus, events line)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus figure in the events calendar, which differs from the +88k in the text.
Down 0.5bps. Yields are holding yesterday's gains.
Core printed in line. No numeric value is given.

risk_factors: Adobe faces intensifying competition and TAM growth accruing to new entrants.
Toshiba's HDD capacity expansion is a supply risk for STX and WDC.
Hot Tokyo CPI and slightly hot Eurozone headline CPI add to inflation risk.
vol_and_positioning: APP is lower in 13 of 14 sessions after another negative sell-side note.
geopolitical: European countries are discussing releasing diesel stockpiles, with France suggesting 100mb of diesel plus crude oil, which pushed crude lower.
SpaceX's plan to build a mobile service using EchoStar spectrum pressures the US wireless carriers.
